title: One calibration query activates a finite adaptive advantage in frozen-versus-renewed dephasing tests
abstract: We quantify a finite calibration resource in one-sided discrimination between a frozen unknown qubit phase and independently renewed dephasing. With five signal queries, dephasing parameter eta=7/10, and one separate noiseless calibration query, an explicit causal strategy has failure probability 0.4657926731886833125. Every parallel five-signal strategy, even with perfect knowledge of the carrier, has failure probability at least 0.46603. The gap is certified by rational matrices and a solver-free verifier. Without calibration, no causal strategy improves the parallel minimax value, so one calibration query is sufficient and minimal at this signal budget. Six parallel signal queries already achieve 0.38442745; the displayed strategy gives no advantage when calibration and signal queries can be freely exchanged at equal cost. A trajectory bound also rules out an improved asymptotic error exponent. The contribution is a small explicit finite-resource construction, not a new phase-estimation framework or a claim of large scientific impact.
